March 15, 2026 | Natural Disasters Summary

Nebraska | USA - Massive wildfires burned over 600,000 acres with 0% containment, becoming the largest fire event in state history and causing fatalities.

Hawaii | USA - Ongoing recovery from Kona storm as flooding, landslides, and infrastructure damage continue across the islands.

Mayurbhanj, Odisha | India - Powerful tornado destroyed over 100 homes, killing 2 people and injuring dozens.

Şanlıurfa and Mardin | Turkey - Heavy rains flooded multiple provinces, damaging homes, farmland, and infrastructure.

Alto Paraná | Paraguay - Severe storm with strong winds damaged homes, injured residents, and caused power outages.

Nicosia and Limassol | Cyprus - Intense storm with 100 km/h winds and 6-7 meter waves caused structural damage and widespread disruptions.

Negros Island | Philippines - Canlaon Volcano eruption sent ash 5 km high, affecting dozens of communities and triggering evacuations.

Catania, Sicily | Italy - Cyclone Iolina brought heavy rain and hail, causing flash flooding and road disruptions.

Ropang, Sumbawa | Indonesia - Flash floods affected over 300 families, damaging homes and infrastructure after prolonged rains.

Cotopaxi Volcano | Ecuador - Glacier collapse triggered by warming caused a large ice mass to break away without volcanic activity.

#SciFeature 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗕𝗨𝗦𝗬 𝗠𝗔𝗥𝗜𝗧𝗜𝗠𝗘 𝗥𝗢𝗨𝗧𝗘𝗦 🚢

The global oil crisis intensified when the Strait of Hormuz, a narrow waterway between the Arabian Peninsula and Iran, was effectively “closed” amid ongoing conflict. As a critical maritime choke point, it handles roughly 20% of the world’s oil supply, making disruptions globally significant.

In the Philippines, we also rely on busy sea lanes and strategic “choke points,” where trade and maritime traffic converge, making them equally vital and vulnerable.

Here’s a map visualizing the bustling shipping routes within and surrounding the Philippine archipelago, transporting passengers and goods to and from the ports across the country. 

From ancient balangays to modern-day ferries and cargo ships, sea transport has always been the lifeblood connecting communities across our 7,000+ islands. Today, thousands of vessels navigate these waters daily, carrying passengers and goods that power our economy and link our lives.

This map shows the total AIS (Automatic Identification System) positions reported by commercial, fishing, oil & gas, passenger, and leisure vessels over a 6-year period, giving us a stunning view of both major and lesser-known maritime highways across the country. Notice how the Port of Manila stands out as the busiest hub, with vibrant routes also extending to and from key cities like Batangas, Cebu, and Cagayan de Oro.
